plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.heading: What this node can load, and what binds it
plugins.lede: Every plugin the engine can load, as its manifest and its code declare it: the version, the plugin API it needs, what it can be and what it declares it can do, with the bindings you can see. "Bound as" is what the configuration uses a plugin for; "can be" is what its code implements. Never a binding's options, which is where credentials live.

error.plugins: The engine's plugin listing is not answering, so what it can load is unknown
error.status: The engine's status endpoint is not answering, so the node line is missing
error.streams: The stream catalog is not answering, so source bindings are shown without their details
error.sinks: The sink list is not answering, so sink bindings are shown without their details

empty.title: No plugins to show
empty.body: The engine reported no plugin it can load and nothing bound to one. A source or sink plugin is a jar on the node's classpath, named in pravaha.sources or pravaha.sinks.

plugins.not_loaded_body: A binding names this plugin, but it is not on the node's classpath. Anything bound to it cannot run.
plugins.unbound: loaded, bound to nothing you can see

not_exposed.title: Not published by the engine
not_exposed.lede: Named here rather than guessed. Each is one answer the engine would have to add.
not_exposed.needs: The engine API that would answer it

start.stream_intro: A stream is a named, typed, unbounded sequence of rows. Pick the one to ask about.

declare.title: Declare a new stream
declare.name: Name
declare.no_event_time: none — no window will ever close
declare.help_before: Event time is the column a window is measured on; out-of-orderness is how late a row may be (ISO-8601) before a window stops waiting for it. This puts the schema in the catalogue; it does not bind a source — rows only arrive once

start.question_after: 's own columns. Edit it freely — it is validated by the engine's planner as you type.
start.query_placeholder: Pick a question above, or write your own
start.register_intro: Registering turns the question into a computation the engine keeps running, and its answer into a view clients read by name.
start.name_rule: Letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.
start.key_legend: Key — what makes a row distinct
start.key_help: For a windowed count, the window and the grouping column together.
start.watch_intro: Open the live view: it shows the view's current rows and every change as the engine commits it, with its weight. If nothing arrives, the usual reasons are that no source is bound to the stream, or — for a windowed question — that the stream has no declared event time, so no window ever closes.
start.see_operations: See it on the operations dashboard

views.no_row_body: The view is correct as of its last commit; nothing in it matches. A row appears when the data that makes it arrives.

states.never_body: A continuous query is registered once and maintained for as long as it is registered. Nothing has been registered on this engine.
states.filtered_body: There are registered queries, but none match what you have typed. The filter is in the URL, so this view is shareable either way.
states.no_retry: Retrying will not help — the request itself was rejected
states.partial_body: {missing} did not answer. The numbers below are lower than the truth, not a complete picture of a smaller thing.
states.unauthorized: You do not have permission to {action}
states.stale_since_load: Not updated since this page loaded.

tail.dropped: {n} rows dropped — this browser is behind the stream

queries.source_stopped_title: A source failed mid-read and is not retried; the view answers at the frontier it reached

diff.queries_failed: The registered queries did not load ({error}); another draft can still be compared.
diff.never_body: Compare this draft with a registered query or another draft: the SQL side by side, both plans with each operator marked added, removed or changed, and what the engine will do with this version.
diff.none_body: There is no registered query and no other draft. Register a query, or open a second draft and write the other version there.
diff.stale_body: The SQL has changed since this comparison, so what is shown is about the previous text.
diff.partial_body: Missing: {missing}. What is shown is complete for what the engine answered.
diff.missing_plan: the plan of {name}, which the engine did not give
diff.missing_schema: the output columns of a side that does not validate, so the column comparison
diff.not_permitted_body: The engine's policy does not let this console read the plan of {name}: {reason}.
diff.not_drawn: The plan could not be drawn: {error}
diff.consequences: What the engine will do with this version
diff.sql_label: SQL diff. The earlier version is on the left, this version on the right.
diff.measured: Measured by the engine for this registered query as a whole:
diff.totals: {rows} rows in · state {held} of {ceiling} · view {view} rows · {subs} subscribers · watermark {watermark}
diff.no_totals: No measured totals: this version has not run, and the engine measures only what runs.
diff.no_totals_registered: No measured totals came with this query's plan.
diff.identical_body: Every operator is the same one on both sides, with the same arguments, columns and state. The list shows differences only.
diff.matching_note: Operators are matched by where they sit in the plan and by kind, never by position in the list: a changed operator is the same kind in the same place with a different label, output columns or state.

op.label: {before} → {after}
op.reorders: emits the same columns in another order

cq.fingerprint_same: {v2} and {v1} have the same fingerprint ({fp}): one computation with two names, one copy of the state.
cq.fingerprint_differs: Two computations: {v1} has fingerprint {left} and {v2} has {right}. Each holds its own state; dropping one leaves the other running.
cq.computation_unknown: Whether this would share {v1}'s computation cannot be told here: a plan is missing.
cq.separate: The plans differ, so the fingerprints will too: registered, this version is a computation of its own, filling its own state from its sources. {v1} keeps running untouched.
cq.may_share: The plans are identical. Registered with {v1}'s keys ({keys}) and retention ({retention}) it would share {v1}'s computation — one state, two names — unless a row filter differs between the two registrations. Other keys or retention make it a second computation. The fingerprint the engine answers with settles it; {v1}'s is {fp}.
cq.may_share_drafts: The plans are identical: registered with the same keys and retention, the two would be one computation.
cq.schema_unknown: The output columns cannot be compared: a side does not validate, or validation is unavailable.
cq.schema_same: The output columns are the same, with the same types.
cq.schema_reordered: The same columns in another order ({before} → {after}): a client reading by position sees them move.
cq.schema_changes: Output columns: {changes}. A client that reads the view by column name sees the difference.
cq.keys_available: {v1}'s key ({keys}) is in this version's output: it can be keyed the same way, and a point query by that key works on both.
cq.keys_missing: {v1}'s key column {missing} is not in this version's output: it cannot be keyed as {v1} is, and a point query by that key would have nothing to look up.
cq.state_same: The state has the same shape: the stateful operators are unchanged.
cq.state_changes: The state changes shape — {changes} — so none of {v1}'s state could serve this version.
cq.not_determinable: Not determinable here: how long this version takes to fill, and how much state it will hold. The engine does not estimate either before registration.

diag.valid: Valid — the engine's planner accepts it

explain.not_drawn: The plan could not be drawn: {error}
explain.not_valid: The query does not validate yet; the plan may be refused.
explain.idle_body: Explain draws the engine's own plan for this query as a graph — operators as nodes, rows flowing left to right.
explain.select: Select an operator (click, or Tab to it and press Enter) for its detail. Arrow keys move between operators.
explain.measured: Measured for the registered query as a whole:
explain.totals: {rows} rows in · state {held} of {ceiling} · view {view} rows · {subscribers} · watermark {watermark}
explain.operator_none: The engine published no numbers for this operator.

op.sampled: Sampled from {n} rows — one in every 1,024 that entered the pipeline is timed at every operator on its path.
op.bottleneck: most of the sampled time goes here

explain.no_bottleneck: No operator stands out yet: nothing has been sampled, or the time is spread evenly.
explain.operators_off: Per-operator numbers are switched off on this node
explain.operators_off_how: Turn them on and re-register the query:
explain.not_running: Per-operator numbers need a registered query

run.caption: Query result
run.statement_before: A continuous-query statement: Run executes it, as you, exactly as
run.statement_after: registers a query that runs until it is dropped.
run.read_before: A one-off read, answered from the views the engine maintains. Nothing is registered. Numbers stay numbers:
run.read_after: is an integer, not the string “40”.
run.idle_body: Run reads a view once. To keep an answer current, register the query instead.
run.truncated: Showing the first {n} rows; the answer was larger. These are the first rows, not a sample.
run.none_body: It ran in {ms} ms and matched nothing. On a stream this often means a window has not closed: a window closes when data says it is over, not when the clock does.

reg.name: Name — what clients put in
reg.name_invalid: Letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.
reg.sinks_failed: The sink list did not load ({error}).
reg.append_only_refused: a query that revises its answer is refused here.
reg.sink_help: Its changes are also written there, retractions included, at least once. A query that revises its answer needs a sink that accepts updates
reg.keys: Key columns — what a row replaces
reg.keys_wait: Keys are chosen by name from the output schema the engine validated. Make the query valid and its columns appear here.
reg.keys_help: A second row with the same key supersedes the first. Two registrations differing only in keys are two computations.
reg.retention_keeps: the view keeps: an ISO-8601 duration such as
reg.retention_after: . Empty takes the engine's default. The engine refuses what it cannot read rather than keeping something else.
reg.refused: The engine's policy does not let this console register a query: {reason}.

PRV-8020.title: The tenant holds as many queries as its quota allows
PRV-8020.fix: Drop a query this tenant no longer needs, or ask an operator to raise max-queries for the tenant under pravaha.tenancy. Registering the same SQL under a name the tenant already holds would still count as a name.

PRV-8021.title: The tenant's views hold as many keys as its state quota allows
PRV-8021.fix: Drop or shorten the retention of a query this tenant no longer needs, so its views hold fewer keys, or ask an operator to raise max-state-keys for the tenant under pravaha.tenancy. Registering SQL identical to a query the tenant already runs shares that computation and needs no new state.

lib.templates: Templates — written against your first stream
lib.snippets: Your snippets — kept in this browser
lib.none: None yet. Select some SQL and save it here; it stays in this browser only.

ai.title: AI models
ai.heading: AI models
ai.lede: The models the assistant asks — several providers and models at once, switched here while the console runs. A change is checked in full, saved, and used by the very next request; a key is named by the variable or file that holds it, never shown.
ai.denied: Only a person the engine gives the admin role may change the assistant's models.
ai.error: Could not ask the engine who you are

not_ready.unrouted: no profile routes to a model

ai.problem: A stored configuration was not applied, and the one in force is kept
ai.drift: The file is at version {stored}; this console is using version {applied}. The console applies a new version within a second of it being stored when it validates here.
ai.changed: Done: {action} {target} — version {version}, in force for the next request.
ai.conflict: Not changed — somebody else changed the configuration since this page was drawn. {detail}
ai.bad_tokens: {what} must be a whole number of tokens, or empty for no limit (not {value}).
ai.bad_seconds: {what} must be a number of seconds (not {value}).
ai.provider_in_use: Remove the models that use this provider first.

field.id_note: The name chains use: letters, digits, dot, underscore, colon, dash.
field.chain_note: Model ids separated by commas; the next is asked only when one is unavailable or rate-limited. Enabled: {models}.
field.key_note: Name the environment variable or the secret file that holds the key — never the key. A value shaped like a key is refused.

models.heading: Models
models.caption: Configured models
models.none_body: Add a provider below, then a model on it, then put the model in a profile's chain.

profiles.heading: Profiles
profiles.lede: A task asks for a profile — draft for drafting a query, explain for explaining one or a refusal. Its chain is tried in order: the first answers, the next is asked only when one is unavailable or rate-limited.
profiles.chain_label: The chain of {profile}, in the order models are asked
profiles.none_body: Set a chain for draft and for explain below; a task whose own profile is missing uses the default one.

providers.heading: Providers
providers.caption: Configured providers
providers.none_body: A provider is where models are reached and how its key is found. Add one below.

types.heading: Provider types this console can use ({n})
types.caption: Provider types, built in and installed

budgets.heading: Budgets
budgets.note: Empty is no limit. A request that could exceed either is refused before it is sent. The daily count is kept per person, by the name the engine signed them in with.

usage.heading: Usage
usage.lede: Tokens from the usage ledger ({n} days kept) and requests from this console's assist log. Read-only.
usage.none_body: Each request the assistant answers is counted here, by model and by person.

changes.heading: Recent changes
changes.caption: Recent changes to the assistant's configuration
changes.none_body: Every change made on this page is listed with who made it and what it was before and after.

access.title: Access
access.heading: What you may do
access.lede: The engine's own answers, asked of its configured policy for you, the person signed in. Read-only: grants live wherever the policy gets them, not here.
access.error: The engine's permissions endpoint is not answering, so what you may do is unknown
access.question: Question
access.read_summary: {views} views and {streams} streams it can see, listed below
access.administer_summary: {n} of the {total} views it can see
access.name: Name
access.filtered_title: The policy applies a row filter; the predicate is not shown here
access.none_body: The policy shows this identity none. Anything it may not see is absent rather than listed with a no, because listing it would disclose that it exists.
access.about_title: What this page is, and is not
access.about_identity: The console reaches the engine as you: every call carries your own session, so these are your permissions, and everything you do is audited as you. A landing chosen in the account menu picks a screen, not a permission.
access.about_hidden: Only what the identity could already see is listed: the engine names no view or stream here that its listing would hide.
access.about_grants: There is nothing to edit. The engine enforces a SecurityPolicy that a deployment implements against its own identity system, and the configured policies have no grants to change.

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.heading: Who asked for what, and what they were told
audit.lede: Every decision the engine's policy made, allows as well as denials, newest first. Every filter is in the address, so a filtered trail is a link.
audit.error: The audit trail could not be read

denied.title: Not permitted
denied.body: The engine refused to show you the audit trail. Reading it is a permission of its own, not a consequence of being allowed to read views, and this attempt has itself been recorded.
denied.fix: An administrator grants it in the engine's policy: under the authenticated policy, a role listed in pravaha.security.audit-readers.
denied.access: See what this identity may do

audit.window: Recorded to {sink}; {retained} of at most {capacity} recent decisions are readable here.
audit.evicted: {n} older ones have left this window.

empty.title: No decision matches
empty.body: Nothing the engine recorded in its readable window matches these filters.

audit.caption: Recorded decisions, newest first
audit.end: The oldest readable decision is on this page.
audit.about_permission: The engine decides who may read this, with a question of its own (SecurityPolicy.mayReadAudit): being entitled to read every view is not being entitled to learn who else read them.
audit.about_recorded: Reading the trail is recorded in it, allowed or refused, with the filter that was asked for.
audit.about_window: The engine keeps a bounded window of recent decisions readable here; with audit set to file, everything older is in the audit file on the node.

never.title: Nothing recorded yet
never.body: The engine is recording, and has no decision to show: none has been made on this node since it started, or every one has been evicted from the window it keeps. Each read, registration and lifecycle action appears here as it is decided.

tenants.title: Tenants
tenants.heading: What each tenant holds, and what it was refused
tenants.lede: The engine's admission quotas, each tenant's use against them, and the registrations refused for going over them since the node started. A quota is checked when a query is registered; nothing running is stopped by it.
tenants.error: The engine's tenants endpoint is not answering, so each tenant's use is unknown
tenants.defaults_note: A tenant with no entry of its own under pravaha.tenancy has these limits.
tenants.scope_all: Every tenant on this node. You may read the audit trail, so the engine shows you every tenant.
tenants.scope_own: Only your own tenant. Seeing every tenant needs permission to read the audit trail; the engine hides other tenants from anyone else.

none.title: No tenant holds anything
none.body: No tenant visible to this identity has registered a query or been refused one. A tenant appears here once it registers or is refused.

tenants.caption: Each tenant's use against its quotas, and the registrations refused for it
tenants.refused_note: Each refusal is also in the audit trail as a denied quota decision, with the tenant as its target.
tenants.about_counts: Queries held counts names, including a name attached to a computation the tenant already runs. Computations counts the distinct computations behind those names: identical SQL shares one within a tenant, and never across tenants.
tenants.about_state: View keys held counts the keys in the views of the tenant's computations. It is checked when a registration would start a computation; a tenant whose views grew past its quota keeps running and is shown over the limit.
tenants.about_null: A limit that is not set is no limit. Zero is a limit: a tenant limited to zero queries can register none.
tenants.about_sharing: The limits are set in the node's configuration under pravaha.tenancy and are read-only here. Refusal counts start from zero when the node restarts.

users.title: Users
users.heading: The people who can sign in
users.lede: The engine's accounts. A person is disabled, never deleted, because the audit trail and the registry name owners by id. Roles decide what the engine lets each person do.
users.error: The engine did not list its users
users.caption: Users
users.roles_note: Separated by commas, e.g. operator, developer.
users.password_note: Checked against the engine's password policy. Tell it to them directly.
users.disabled: {user} is disabled, and their sessions are ended.
users.bad_status: A person is either active or disabled.

keys.title: API keys
keys.heading: Every API key
keys.lede: Every key the engine holds, by its key id: the handle the audit trail uses. A key's secret is never shown here; the engine keeps only a hash of it.
keys.error: The engine did not list its keys

report.title: What wants attention
report.error: The engine's key report did not answer, so the keys are listed without it.
report.unused_note: Never used, or not lately: candidates to revoke.
report.expiring_note: Expire soon: rotate them before they do.
report.superseded_note: Rotated, and still inside their overlap.

none.title: No API keys
none.body: Nobody has made a key yet. People make their own on their account page.

keys.caption: Every API key

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.heading: Every open session
sessions.lede: Everyone signed in, and where. Ending a session takes effect on that person's next request.
sessions.error: The engine did not list its sessions
sessions.caption: Every open session

lanes.title: Lanes
lanes.heading: Where every query runs
lanes.lede: Each query runs on a lane of its own or shares one. Under auto, a node's first queries each own a lane and later ones share; nothing is moved while it runs.
lanes.mode_auto: auto — a lane each until {n} queries are hosted, then shared
lanes.caption: Every registered query and the lane it runs on
lanes.error: The engine did not say where queries run
lanes.rebalance_lede: Room left under auto-from — by dropped queries — is used only by new registrations until an administrator rebalances. A rebalance moves shared queries, oldest first, onto lanes of their own, one at a time and without losing an answer (a blue/green replacement with the SQL unchanged).
lanes.confirm: Move these queries onto lanes of their own, one at a time?
lanes.room: Room for {n} more on lanes of their own
lanes.nothing: Nothing to move: no room under auto-from, or no query is sharing.
lanes.running: A rebalance is running; this page shows its progress when reloaded.
lanes.admins_only: Only an administrator can rebalance lanes.

operations.heading: Is everything healthy — and if not, where?
operations.no_watermark_title: No row with an event time has arrived
operations.nothing_body: No query is near its state ceiling, stopped, or behind in event time.
operations.metrics_down: The engine's metrics endpoint is not answering
operations.metrics_down_body: {error} — the per-query numbers below come from the registry alone until it does.

col.commit_title: Mean time from applying a commit to the last subscriber and sink having it, between two scrapes
col.checkpoint_title: Age of the last stored checkpoint, and failures
col.blocked_title: The share of wall clock a writer into this query's lanes spent with nowhere to put a row. On a shared lane it counts every writer into that lane, the neighbours' included.
col.inbox_title: Rows queued into the lane and not yet taken, out of what the inbox holds. An instantaneous gauge: a burst between two scrapes is invisible.

operations.gauge_label: state held as a share of its ceiling

empty.title: No queries registered
empty.body: Once one is, its throughput, state and lag are here.

operations.reconciled:
Per-query meters are reconciled with the registry every 15 s, so a query registered a moment
  ago shows “not published yet” for up to that long.

chart.rate_label: Rows in per second, per query
chart.rate_caption_after: , per query, from this console's 1 s scrapes. Window: since this page opened, up to 5 min.
chart.state: State held, as a share of its ceiling
chart.state_label: State held as a fraction of ceiling, per query
chart.state_caption: , 0–100 %, fixed scale so queries compare. At 100 % a query is refused (PRV-4001) unless spilling is on.

not_measured.title: Not measured by the engine
not_measured.lede: Shown as absent rather than as zero: the engine does not measure these, so there is no honest number to draw.

operations.blocked_label: share of time the lane had nowhere to put a row
operations.bottleneck: Most of the time goes into {op} — open the plan

lanes.heading: Shared lanes
lanes.lede: A lane's own backpressure, which is a different question from a query's: every query hosted on a shared lane queues behind one inbox, so a query can read high above because a neighbour's writer is the one waiting.
lanes.name: lane {n}
lanes.gauge_label: share of time this lane had nowhere to put a row
lanes.none_body: Every query here holds a lane and an inbox of its own, so there is no shared lane to be blocked. That is not a table of idle lanes: there are none. By default (pravaha.lane.multiplex.enabled: auto) a node starts sharing lanes once it hosts 64 queries, keeping a lane apiece while isolation is cheap; true shares from the first query, false never.
lanes.where: Where each query runs, and rebalancing →

operators.on: Per-operator numbers are on for this node, so a query's plan carries rows, state, watermark and a sampled self time for each of its operators.
operators.off: Per-operator numbers are off for this node (pravaha.metrics.operators), so a plan carries none. The counters are built into a query's stages when it is compiled, so turning it on means re-registering the query.
operators.unknown: Whether per-operator numbers are on for this node is not published by it, so a plan carrying none could be either answer.
operators.how: How to read a plan's numbers

query.fingerprint_title: The canonical plan this name resolves to. Two names with the same fingerprint are one computation.

name.title: pravāha — that which flows
name.p1_flow: : a river's flow, continuous and directional. Not the water, which is always different water — the
name.p1_after: , which is the thing that persists.
name.p2: Which is what a stream is, and what makes streaming hard to reason about. The rows are gone the moment they pass. What you keep is the answer they changed, and the discipline is knowing which answers a row can still change and which it cannot.
name.p3_question: can anything still arrive that changes this?
name.p3_after: — is what watermarks answer, what retention rests on, and what decides when a window may close.

different.incremental_body: A change is a delta. Z-sets carry weights, so a correction is a retraction and an insert — never a rescan.
different.event_time_body: A window closes when the data says it is over, not when the clock does. Late rows correct the answer rather than being lost.
different.shared_body: Two people asking the same question get one computation and one copy of the state — matched on the normalised plan, not the SQL text.
different.bounded_body: Every operator that could grow without limit has a bound, and a query with no bound is refused at plan time rather than at 3am.
different.heading: Not a job you submit. A question it keeps answering.
different.desc: A batch engine recomputes. A stream processor forgets. This one keeps the answer, and moves it by exactly what each row changes.

does.protocol_body: Arrow Flight SQL for query, prepare, register and subscribe. Both SDKs and the CLI speak it; so does any Flight client.

figure.caption: FIG. 01 — ONE QUESTION, KEPT ANSWERED
figure.heading: A row arrives, and the answer changes by exactly that much
figure.said_1: Rows arrive from the sources a query reads — a Kafka topic, a Postgres change feed, an Aerospike namespace, a Delta table, a JDBC database, files — and each carries a weight: +1 for a row that is now true, −1 for one that was true and is not. An update is both, the old row withdrawn and the new one inserted. The engine applies them a commit at a time, and the answer changes by exactly that much: a total that read 900 steps back to 90 without anything being rescanned.
figure.said_2: The same weights go out again. A subscriber is sent each commit as it happens, a point read looks one key up in the answer the engine keeps, a sink writes the changes to a Delta table, a JDBC database or a Kafka topic, and the console shows them — ways of reading one computation, not copies of it.

diagram.title: How Pravaha works
diagram.desc: Rows from your stores feed declared streams. A continuous query, registered once, turns every change into a Z-set delta and maintains a keyed view. The view is read by key, subscribed to commit by commit, or written to a sink. Checkpoints and the registry journal let a restart resume.

l.or_captured_from_a_change: or captured from a change log
l.one_cut_across_every_input: one cut across every input · a restart resumes, it does not replay from scratch

how.1: A stream is declared — its schema, which column is event time, how late its rows may arrive — and bound to a source plugin that reads one of your stores.
how.2: A continuous query is registered once, under a name and a key. Calcite parses and plans it; Pravaha's own operators run it, as generated code, on a lane — and identical questions share one computation.
how.3: Every row becomes a change with a weight: +1 for a row appearing, −1 for one withdrawn. Operators transform changes into changes, so the work is proportional to what changed.
how.4: The watermark — how far event time has certainly advanced — closes windows. A late row inside the allowed lateness reopens a window as a retraction of the old answer and the corrected one, in one commit.
how.5: The view is the answer, maintained and keyed. Applications read it by key over Flight SQL or the PostgreSQL wire protocol, subscribe to its commits, or have the node write each commit to a sink. Checkpoints cut every input at one point, so a restart resumes.

dlq.title: Dead letters — {name}
dlq.heading: Records this query could not decode
dlq.retention_title: pravaha.dlq.max-bytes, .max-entries and .max-age. Past the bound the oldest are evicted and counted, never dropped quietly.
dlq.evicted: {n} older entries ({bytes} bytes) have been evicted by retention and are gone. The bound is {bound}: raise pravaha.dlq.max-bytes, or drain the queue more often.
dlq.replay_done: {done} replayed as new rows at the query's current frontier; {again} failed to decode again and went back on the queue.
dlq.semantics: A replayed record is a new row at the query's current frontier, not a rewind: nothing is re-read and no earlier answer is recomputed. A record that fails to decode again goes back on the queue as a new entry rather than being retried.
dlq.choose_one: Choose the dead letter {id} to replay

none.title: {name} has no dead letters
none.body: Every record its sources have sent has decoded. A record that cannot be decoded is written here with its bytes and its reason, and the source reads on.

unconfigured.title: This node keeps no dead letters
unconfigured.body: pravaha.dlq.directory is not set, so a record a source cannot decode stops that source rather than being kept. That is not an empty queue: it is the queue being switched off, and a bad record ends the poll and takes the rest of the feed with it.

error.none_chosen: Choose which dead letters to replay. Replaying a whole queue is not offered: a queue is usually a mix of causes, and most of it is still malformed.

cutover.title: Replacing {name}
cutover.heading: Replacing {name}
cutover.no_eta: There is no estimate and no percentage here, and there will not be one: a source does not say how much history it holds, so there is no total to be a share of. What is below is measured — rows read, the rate, the partitions that have reached the live stream, and how far behind the running version the candidate's event time is.
cutover.candidate_title: The fingerprint of the computation being prepared.
cutover.replacing_title: The fingerprint of the computation serving this name now.

none.title: {name} is not being replaced
none.body: A blue/green replacement runs a new version of this query beside the running one, reads the history its sources still hold, splices onto the live stream where the running version has reached, and waits for you to move the name across. Until you do, the name answers exactly what it answers now.
none.note: The console does not start a replacement from a blank form: the new version is SQL, and SQL is written in the workbench, where the planner refuses what it cannot run before anything is registered.

progress.heading: The backfill
progress.live_rows: Records read from the live stream

rollback.heading: The rollback window
rollback.open: The version this replaced is retained until {until}. Until then, rolling back puts it back.
rollback.open_note: Rolling back ends every subscription to the name, as the cutover did: a reader subscribes again and starts from a fresh snapshot.
rollback.closed_note: The window ran to {until} and the version this replaced is no longer retained. There is nothing to roll back to; going back now means registering the old SQL again and backfilling it.
rollback.over: This replacement is {state}, so there is no window to keep open.
rollback.not_yet: Nothing has been cut over yet, so there is nothing to roll back. A window opens when the name moves to the candidate, and its length is the rollback.retention this replacement was started with.

controls.heading: Controls
controls.cutover_title: Move the name to the candidate, at a position both versions have consumed exactly.
controls.cutover_early: The candidate has not read all of the history yet. Cutting over now is refused by the engine, because the two versions would be at different positions in their input.
controls.rollback_title: Put the replaced version back, while it is still retained.
controls.rollback_gone: The version this replaced is no longer retained, so there is nothing to roll back to.
controls.note: The ceiling may be lowered while the backfill runs and not raised above the one it was started with; the engine refuses a raise rather than the console quietly clamping it. Pause keeps what has been read. Abandon ends a replacement that has not cut over and releases the candidate.
controls.note_cut_over: The name answers the candidate now. Rolling back puts the replaced version back while it is still retained, and Finish releases it early — after which there is no rollback.
controls.note_over: This replacement is over. Nothing here can be undone from this screen; a new version means a new replacement, and its own backfill.

cutover.refused_title: This console's identity may not act on this replacement
cutover.refused_body: Starting, throttling, cutting over and rolling back all need the administer permission on this name, and the engine's policy says: {reason}

confirm.cutover_title: Cut over to the new version of “{name}”?
confirm.cutover_body: Every reader of {name} sees the candidate's answer after this, and every open subscription ends with PRV-4019 and has to subscribe again. The replaced version is kept for the rollback window and no longer.
confirm.rollback_title: Roll “{name}” back to the replaced version?
confirm.rollback_body: Every reader of {name} sees the old answer again after this, and every open subscription ends and has to subscribe again. The candidate is released.

history.heading: Who has served this name
history.not_carried: The engine records who served this name from which seam, and this console did not get an answer for it — the trail comes from the engine's HTTP surface rather than from the status above, and that call did not answer. An empty list here would read as “nobody has”, which is a different thing, so nothing is listed.
history.none_title: Nothing has served this name but the version running now
history.none_body: A cutover adds an entry here: the fingerprint that took over, and the position it took over at.

done.cutover: {name} now answers the new version. The replaced one is kept for the rollback window.
done.finish: The replacement of {name} is finished and the replaced version has been released. There is no rollback now.
done.abandon: The replacement of {name} has been abandoned and the candidate released. The running version never stopped.
done.pause: The backfill of {name} is paused. What it has read is kept.
done.resume: The backfill of {name} is reading again.
done.throttle: The backfill now reads at most {rate} records a second.
done.start: A candidate is running beside {name}, reading history. The name still answers the version it answered before.

error.rate: “{rate}” is not a number of records a second.
error.keys: “{keys}” is not a list of key columns: name them, or give their output ordinals.

start.heading: Start one
start.note: The new version's SQL, as it will run. This form does not check it — the planner is the engine's, and a second opinion here would be a weaker one — so write and validate it first:
start.workbench: open this query in the workbench
start.sql_help: Prefilled with what is running now. The engine refuses a candidate that normalises to the computation already running: that would be a cutover to itself.
start.keys_help: By name, or as output ordinals. The running version's keys, prefilled.
start.backfill_help: Starting at the live position leaves the candidate with empty state, which is right only for a query whose answer does not depend on history.
start.rate_help: Records a second. Blank for none. It can be lowered later and never raised above this.

debug.title: Debugging {name}
debug.heading: Debugging {name}
debug.refused_title: This identity may not debug this query
debug.refused_body: A fork shows the query's SQL, the rows going into it and what every operator is holding, which is more than reading its view shows and more than reading its plan shows. So it takes the same permission dropping the query takes, and the engine says: {reason}
debug.refused_access: What this console is allowed to do

none.title: {name} is not being debugged
none.body: A debug session runs this query a second time under inspection. It starts from one of the checkpoints this node still retains, so it begins with the state the query actually had, and it reads the same sources from the positions that checkpoint recorded — the same rows, in order, from that moment on. You drive it: one row, ten rows, on to the next commit, on to a watermark, or on until a column of the view crosses a value.

absence.sink: No sink is attached. A sink is opened for a registration, and a fork is not one, so there is nothing to switch off and nothing to leave on.
absence.view: Nothing can read the fork's view. It is named for the session and never put in the catalogue, so no name resolves to it and no subscription reaches it.
absence.lanes: Its lanes are its own. A fork never joins a shared lane, even where the live query is on one — so the query it forked from goes on as it was.

checkpoints.heading: Where a fork can start
checkpoints.none_title: There is no checkpoint of {name} to fork from
checkpoints.none_body: Three different things read the same from here — this node does not checkpoint at all, this query has not taken one yet, and every one it took has been pruned — so nothing here guesses between them. Ask for a fork and the engine tells them apart by name (PRV-8011).

fork.note: Positions this node still retains: {n}. A fork is a whole second copy of the query — its lanes, its arena, its operator state and a reader per partition — so a node holds only a few at once and releases one nobody has touched.
fork.newest: the newest this node still retains
fork.checkpoint_help: Leaving this alone asks the engine for the newest one at the moment you press the button, which is not necessarily the newest one on this list: a node prunes while a page is open.

open.heading: Sessions already open on this query
open.note: Each is a second copy of the query, held until somebody ends it or the node's own timeout releases it.
open.entry: from checkpoint {checkpoint} · steps {steps} · rows consumed {rows} · last touched {at}

gone.title: That session is over
gone.body: The engine knows no session {id}. It was ended, or nobody touched it for long enough that the node released it — a session holds a whole second copy of the query, so it is not kept indefinitely.

banner.body: Sinks are disabled, and not by a setting: this fork never opened one. Nothing outside it can read its view, and the query it forked from is running untouched — if that query looks wrong, this session is not why.

chip.id_title: The session's id. It is in this page's address, so a link to it reaches the same session.

step.heading: Step
step.spec_help: row · rows:N · commit · watermark:<nanos> · until:<column>:<op>:<value>. A breakpoint is one column of the view against one value, with = != < <= > >=, and nothing more: a second expression language that is nearly SQL's would disagree with SQL somewhere, in the one tool you opened because you already had a wrong answer.

report.heading: What each step did
report.nothing_yet: Nothing has been stepped yet. Each step answers four questions at once: what came in, what every operator did with it, what the view did, and where event time now stands.
report.no_rows: No row entered: this step moved event time rather than the input.
report.tail: {rows} rows consumed in all · the view holds {view} rows · watermark {watermark}

state.heading: What the operators are holding
state.note: Reading changes nothing: a join's index is walked without evicting from it, an aggregate is read without emitting it, and the read happens on the lane that owns the memory rather than beside it.
state.none_title: This fork holds no operator state
state.none_body: A plan of scans, filters and projections keeps nothing between rows. State appears here when the plan has an aggregate, a join or a window.

page.heading: Inside {operator}
page.key_help: Leave it empty for the page as the walk finds it. A page is bounded on the way in as well as out, because an unbounded page of a join holding ten million rows takes the node down.
page.no_key: This operator is holding nothing under {value}.
page.empty_body: It has state to hold and has not been given anything to hold yet.
page.windows: A windowed aggregate shows the windows it has fired and is still retaining, not the ones still filling. The only way to read an open window's answer is to fire it, and a debugger that published a window early would have changed the query it was asked about.

view.heading: The fork's view
view.note: Its weights are Z-set weights: an update is the old row withdrawn at −1 and the new one inserted at +1, which is why one arriving row makes two changes.
view.none_body: The checkpoint this session started from held no rows for this view, and nothing stepped so far has added one.

fixture.heading: Export it as a test
fixture.note: The session becomes a JUnit fixture: the schema of every stream the query reads, its SQL and key columns, the rows this session consumed in order with their weights and event times, the watermarks it pushed, and the view to expect. It needs nothing from this node and goes on working when the state format changes.
fixture.name: Name it after what it reproduces
fixture.name_help: It becomes the test class's name, so “user 42 goes negative” becomes User42GoesNegativeFixtureTest.
fixture.expectation: What it asserts is the answer over those rows from empty, not over the history before the checkpoint — and the number in it was produced at export time by running the script through an empty copy of the query, rather than copied from this fork and hoped for. Copy the file into the repository at the path above; nothing was written to disk here.

end.heading: End the session
end.note: Releases the second copy of the query. Nothing read it and nothing wrote, so there is nothing to undo.

done.fork: Forked. Session {id} is yours to step.
done.end: Session {id} is over and its copy of the query is released.

error.checkpoint: “{checkpoint}” is not a checkpoint id; a checkpoint id is a whole number, and leaving it alone asks for the newest one this node still retains.

competitive.title: Competitive landscape
competitive.heading: Competitive landscape
competitive.lede: Where Pravaha stands among the kinds of product that do part of its job — scored by category, not vendor — and, for every row, how the others meet the need and how Pravaha does, with the record that proves it. Losses included.

s.behind: Where Pravaha is partial or behind, and why

competitive.caption: Capabilities, by category of product, against Pravaha
competitive.missing: The comparison is read from docs/COMPETITIVE_LANDSCAPE.md, which this installation does not carry.

session.expired: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
session.must_change: Your password must be changed before anything else; open /account/password.

csrf.refused: This request did not carry this session's form token. Reload the page and try again.
csrf.what: a request without its form token
csrf.detail: Every change made through the console carries a token only a page from this console knows, so another site cannot make one on your behalf. This one arrived without it, or with an old one — usually because the page was open from before a sign-in. Nothing was changed.

account.title: Your account
account.heading: Your account
account.me_error: The engine did not say who you are

password.title: Change password
password.heading: Change your password
password.forced: Your password must be changed before you can do anything else.
password.forced_flash: Choose a new password to carry on.
password.rules: The engine's policy decides what it accepts: by default at least 12 characters, from three of lower case, upper case, digits and symbols, and none of your last five.
password.differ: The two new passwords are not the same.
password.policy: The engine did not accept that password: {detail}
password.wrong_current: Your current password was not accepted.

landing.title: Where you land
landing.note: Where signing in takes you, remembered for you on this browser. It picks a screen; it grants nothing.

keys.title: Your API keys
keys.lede: A key lets a program call the engine as you, with the roles you give it — never more than your own. It is shown once, when it is made, and the engine keeps only a hash of it.
keys.error: The engine did not list your keys

none.title: You have no API keys
none.body: Make one below for a program that needs to call the engine as you.

keys.caption: Your API keys
keys.name: Name
keys.create_note: At most 365 days. Rotating a key makes a successor with the same roles; the old one keeps working for 7 days, then expires.
keys.widen: A key can carry only roles you hold: {detail}
keys.roles_note: The key's roles, from your own. Administration is left off unless you tick it.

sessions.title: Your sessions
sessions.lede: Everywhere you are signed in. A session ends after 30 minutes idle or 12 hours, and at most three are open at once.
sessions.error: The engine did not list your sessions
sessions.caption: Your sessions

issued.once: Copy it now. It is shown this once and never again: the engine keeps only a hash of it.
issued.reset_note: Single use, for an hour. Hand it to the person directly, not by email; they set a new password with it at /login/reset.

denied.title: Not permitted
denied.body: The engine did not allow your account to see this. Administering people needs its admin role.

reset.title: Set a new password
reset.heading: Set a new password with a reset token
reset.lede: An administrator gave you a reset token. It works once, for an hour; setting a password with it ends every session you had open.
reset.invalid: That reset token is not valid: it was mistyped, has been used, or is more than an hour old. Ask for another.

governance.search: Search names, descriptions, owners and tags
governance.caption: Governed objects you may see
governance.visibility_note: Only what the engine lets you USE is listed; a search never shows an object you may not see.
governance.revoked: Revoked {privilege} on {object} from {grantee}; it takes effect at their next read.

off.title: The catalogue is off on this engine
off.body: Who may do what is decided by the engine's configured policy, and there are no grants to show or change. An administrator turns it on with

none.title: Nothing you may see
none.body: The catalogue shows the objects in namespaces you may use. Ask an owner for USE on a namespace.

grants.title: Grants
grants.heading: Who may do what, to which object
grants.lede: Grants live in the engine. Each change here is asked of the engine as you, needs MANAGE on the object, and is recorded in the audit trail.
grants.object_note: A full name (acme.sales.revenue), a namespace, or a view as you would write it.

policies.title: Policies
policies.heading: Row filters and masks
policies.lede: A grant says whether someone may read; a policy says what they are shown. Each change is asked of the engine as you, which checks the expression and needs MANAGE where you bind it.
policies.caption: Row filters and masks you may see
policies.none: No row filters or masks you may see.
policies.bind_note: One of an object (MANAGE on it) or a tag (MANAGE on the tenant: every object carrying it, now and later).
policies.expression_note: Columns, pure functions, CASE, CAST, and session_attribute('claim'), current_user(), is_member('role'). Nothing is narrowed until it is bound.
policies.created: {name} created; bind it to take effect.
policies.none_on_object: No row filter or mask reaches it.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.lede: An alert watches a continuous query's view: a key fires when its row enters the answer and clears when it leaves. Pausing, snoozing and dedupe change what is said, never what is true.
alerts.caption: Alerts you may see
alerts.paused: {name} is paused: it keeps following its view and says nothing until resumed.
alerts.resumed: {name} is resumed; what changed while it was quiet is sent now.
alerts.snoozed: {name} is snoozed for {duration}; what changes meanwhile is sent when it ends.
alerts.acked: {name}: {count} firing keys acknowledged; they are not reminded about until they fire again.

off.title: This engine serves no alerts
off.body: Alerts are served by a node with its alert service on. An administrator turns it on with

none.title: No alerts you may see
none.body: Create one with CREATE ALERT <name> ON <view> NOTIFY <channel>, in the workbench or with pravaha alert create.

detail.up_to_date: every channel is up to date
detail.actions: Quiet it, or say you have seen it
detail.actions_note: Pause, resume and snooze need MODIFY on the alert, as does acknowledging; the engine decides.
detail.no_keys: No key is in the condition, and none has fired.
